title: Future: will, going to and plans
point: Use will for decisions made on the spot and promises, be going to for intentions and things you can see coming, and the present progressive for fixed plans.

sentences.ja: 電話が鳴ってる。私が出るよ。
sentences.text: The phone's ringing. I'll get it.
sentences.note: A decision made right now takes "will"; "get it" means answer the phone or the door.

sentences.ja: この夏はバイトでお金を貯めるつもり。
sentences.text: I'm going to save up money from my part-time job this summer.

sentences.ja: 明日の午後、歯医者の予約があるんだ。
sentences.text: I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow afternoon.
sentences.note: An appointment already on the calendar takes the present progressive.

sentences.ja: 空を見て。雨が降りそうだ。
sentences.text: Look at the sky. It's going to rain.

sentences.note: Offers made on the spot use "will", not "going to".

sentences.ja: 彼らは来月結婚します。
心配しないで。誰にも言わないから。
sentences.text: Don't worry. I won't tell anyone.

sentences.ja: 来学期は心理学の授業を取るつもりです。
sentences.text: I'm going to take a psychology class next semester.

sentences.ja: このペースだと、締め切りに間に合わないと思う。
sentences.text: At this rate, I don't think we'll make the deadline.
sentences.note: Say "I don't think we'll" rather than "I think we won't".
